claims.text: A threat model is a written list of what could go wrong with a system's security, where in its data flow it could happen, and what is done about each case, made before an attacker finds the gaps. A penetration test is a team attacking the running system on purpose to find holes.
claims.source_hint: glossary threat-model; outline item 1; docs/design/threat-model.md @ stage-4 lines 1-9

claims.text: A trust boundary is a place in the data flow where data passes between parts that trust each other to different degrees: browser to Gateway, a service to PostgreSQL, Payments to the payment gateway.
claims.source_hint: glossary trust-boundary; outline item 2; threat-model.md @ stage-4 headings lines 11, 27, 42

claims.text: STRIDE, the checklist threat-model.md uses, names six kinds of threat to ask about at each boundary: spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, elevation of privilege.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/threat-model.md @ stage-4 lines 4-6

claims.text: threat-model.md was written at stage-4 for the stage-3 data flow (Compose and staging); each boundary is asked all six STRIDE kinds; each threat gets a control or a finding decided fix / accept with a reason / defer to a named plan; only rows with something to say are kept.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/threat-model.md @ stage-4 lines 3-9

claims.text: Browser boundary, spoofing: the API and Payments check each token's signature, issuer (who issued it, Keycloak), audience (which API it is meant for) and expiry with AddJwtBearer; Caddy and the Gateway check no token.

claims.text: On staging the Gateway serves HTTPS with a certificate from the lab's own CA; in Compose the app's requests reach Caddy over plain HTTP, on a developer's machine. The Gateway reaches the api and Payments Pods over plain HTTP (P5).

claims.text: A PostgreSQL role is the account a client signs in as, with its own permissions; a superuser skips every permission check, so it can connect to every database; the postgres image creates the POSTGRES_USER user as a superuser.

claims.text: Decisions for a finding: fix when the threat is likely or costly and the fix affordable now; accept when the reason holds and names when to look again; defer when a planned change will soon reach the same place.

claims.text: A model made from the data flow finds design findings while the fix is still a planned change; a test at the end finds them only after the design is built, and a test report records no decision such as accepting P5.

claims.text: A threat model lists threats found at the boundaries the team drew, each with a decision; deferred and accepted findings stay open, and the model covers only the data flow it was made from.
